title: Finitely many finite separable extensions embed into one finite Galois extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$, and let $L_1,\dots,L_n$ be field extensions of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] which are finite ($\dim_kL_i<\infty$) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then there are a field extension $L/k$ and homomorphisms of $k$-algebras $\tau_i:L_i\to L$ ($i=1,\dots,n$) such that $L/k$ is finite ($\dim_kL<\infty$), separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal: for every $\beta\in L$ the minimal polynomial of $\beta$ over $k$ (as in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]) is a product of polynomials of degree one in $L[T]$. (That is, $L/k$ is a finite Galois extension, Stacks, Fields, Definition 09I0, receiving every $L_i$.)

source.place: Fields, Lemma 09DT (fields-lemma-normal-closure, line 2086: existence of the normal closure of a finite extension) and Lemma 0EXM (fields-lemma-normal-closure-galois, line 2704: the normal closure of a finite separable extension is Galois); a finite separable extension containing copies of all L_i is obtained from Fields, Lemma 09GU (fields-lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure, line 1023: embed each L_i into an algebraic closure) and Lemma 09HC (fields-lemma-separable-elements, line 1435: the compositum of the images is separable). Used in the proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (more-morphisms.tex lines 12064-12066: 'Choose a finite Galois extension L/kappa(s) such that there exist kappa(s)-embeddings L_i -> L')

proof.text: A Galois extension to work in. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois] (1) there is a field extension $\Omega/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] such that $\Omega$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed] and $\Omega/k$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; by part (2) of the same node, applied with $k'=k$, the extension $\Omega/k$ is moreover normal: for every $\alpha\in\Omega$ the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $\Omega[T]$. So $\Omega/k$ is Galois (Stacks, Fields, Definition 09I0).

source.place: Fields, Definition 09I0 (fields-definition-galois, line 2654); the separable closure as in the cited node

proof.text: Embedding each $L_i$. For each $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ the extension $L_i/k$ is separable algebraic by hypothesis and $\Omega$ is separably closed (step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] there is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $\sigma_i:L_i\to\Omega$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma 09GU (fields-lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure, line 1023), in its separable form as stated in the cited node

proof.text: A finite Galois subextension containing the images of bases. Since $\dim_kL_i<\infty$, choose a $k$-basis $e_{i1},\dots,e_{id_i}$ of $L_i$ for each $i$, and let $S=\{\sigma_i(e_{ij}):1\le i\le n,\ 1\le j\le d_i\}\subseteq\Omega$, a finite set (empty if $n=0$). Since $\Omega/k$ is Galois (step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] gives a subfield $L$ with $k\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$ and $S\subseteq L$ such that $L/k$ is finite ($\dim_kL<\infty$), separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal (the minimal polynomial over $k$ of every $\beta\in L$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $L[T]$). Being a subfield of $\Omega$ containing $k$, $L$ is a field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Fields, Lemma 09DT (fields-lemma-normal-closure, line 2086) and Lemma 0EXM (fields-lemma-normal-closure-galois, line 2704), through the cited node

proof.text: The maps $\tau_i$. Let $x\in L_i$ and write $x=\sum_jc_je_{ij}$ with $c_j\in k$. Since $\sigma_i$ is $k$-linear, $\sigma_i(x)=\sum_jc_j\sigma_i(e_{ij})$, a $k$-linear combination of elements of $S\subseteq L$; as $L$ is a subfield of $\Omega$ containing $k$, it is closed under such combinations, so $\sigma_i(x)\in L$. Hence $\sigma_i(L_i)\subseteq L$, and $\sigma_i$ with its codomain restricted to $L$ is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $\tau_i:L_i\to L$ (the operations and the map from $k$ of $L$ are those of $\Omega$). Together with step 3, $L$ and $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n$ are as claimed. (For $n=0$ the statement asks only for $L$, and step 3 with $S=\emptyset$ gives one, e.g. $L=k$.)

lean.statement: theorem finite_galois_receiving_separable_extensions (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (L : Fin n → Type v) [hfield : ∀ i, Field (L i)] [halgebra : ∀ i, Algebra k (L i)] (hfinite : ∀ i, letI := hfield i; letI := halgebra i; FiniteDimensional k (L i)) (hseparable : ∀ i, letI := hfield i; letI := halgebra i; Algebra.IsSeparable k (L i)) : ∃ (K : Type (max u v)) (hK : Field K) (aK : Algebra k K), letI := hK letI := aK FiniteDimensional k K ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k K ∧ (∀ β : K, ((minpoly k β).map (algebraMap k K)).Splits) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, letI := hfield i; letI := halgebra i; Nonempty ((L i) →ₐ[k] K))
